Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 
Ritika Chandwani 
TY BTech IT 
 
 
Online Coding Assessment (90 mins): 
Only CS/IT and EXTC students with a CGPA of 7.0+ were allowed to take the test. The 
online assessment was scheduled for 6th November 2022 at 3 pm. The test was proctored and 
was held on the  HackerEarth platform. The test was designed to be of total 90 marks 
There were 10 MCQs on CS Fundamentals (each of 4 marks). Some of them were pretty 
basic and a few of them were of medium level. 
Then there were two coding questions each having 10 Test Cases. 
1. Maximum Quirkiness (20 marks): 
Given an array A of size N, find the pair of index {i,j} such that quirkiness between 
them is maximum and return the maximum quirkiness. 
The Quirkiness of two indexes i and j is defined as Q( i, j ) = Sum of array elements 
from index i to index j + constant*(j-i) 
Q(i,j) = ∑
𝐴𝑛+ 𝑐(𝑗−𝑖)
𝑗
𝑛=𝑖
 
Where An is the sum of array elements from index i to j and j>i. 
Also, indexing starts from 1 for the given array and the constant value was given. 
Return the maximum quirkiness for the given array. 
 
Example: Consider N = 4, c=2, A= [4,1,2,-2] 
If we take i=1,j=3 we get quirkiness = 7+ 2*(3-1) = 11 
This is the maximum quirkiness across all pairs of indexes. So, return 11. 
 
Approach:  
I started with the brute force approach using three nested loops. One loop for 
choosing ith index, another loop for choosing the jth index and third loop for 
calculating the sum of array elements between i and j. And each time calculating 
quirkiness and returning the maximum value.  
Of course, this led to TLE as time complexity was O(n3). Though I was able to pass 
5/10 test cases. 
 
Then, one important thing to note  here is that we need the maximum sum of the array 
elements between i and j and also the maximum difference between i and j to 
maximize the quirkiness. So, I tried finding out the maximum sum subarray. This 
reminded me of Kadane’s algorithm. So, using Kadane’s algorithm, I found out 
maximum sum between any two indices and then found out the quirkiness for those 
indices and returned the value. Although in most cases, quirkiness will be maximum 
where sum of subarray is maximum, it may happen that because of the indices

2 
 
difference, the quirkiness may not be maximum. With this approach, I got 7/10 test 
cases passed. 
 
Further, I went on to thinking how to simultaneously consider the index position too. I 
tried modifying Kadane’s algorithm, by taking into consideration the start and end 
index difference, but I was running short on time. So, I decided to switch questions 
and first try solving the next question and come back, if time permits. But, eventually, 
I couldn’t solve it any further before the time. 
 
 
2. Collecting Coins (30 marks):  
John is playing a battle game that consists of N heroes and M monsters. The power of 
heroes and the monsters are represented by arrays H and M respectively. A hero can 
defeat a monster if his power is greater than or equal to the power of the monster. On 
defeating a monster, the hero gains a certain amount of coins corresponding to that 
monster. The coins after defeating a particular monster are represented by an array C 
of size M. Now, John is curious to know how many coins each hero can collect by 
defeating any monster in the game. Return an array of N integers containing coins 
earned by each hero. The health of a hero doesn’t get reduced after defeating a 
monster. Also, a monster can be defeated by multiple heroes. 
 
Example:  
Let N = 5, M = 4,  A = [1,3,5,2,4], B = [1,4,2,9],  C = [1,2,8,4] 
The first hero can defeat only the 1st monster, so he gains only 1 coin. 
The second hero can defeat the 1st and 3rd monsters, so he gains 1+8=9 coins. 
Similarly, the third, fourth, and fifth heroes gain 11, 9 and11 coins respectively. 
Return: [ 1, 9, 11, 9, 11 ] 
 
Approach: 
Again, I started with brute force, simply using two nested loops, traverse the hero’s 
array, and compare its power with each monster, whenever the hero’s power is greater 
than or equal to the monster, add coins for that hero and finally return the array. 
With this approach, I got 5/10 test cases correct. 
 
Now, I had to optimize this approach and get the answer in less time complexity. For 
this, since we need to find only those heroes whose power was greater than the 
monster’s power, I thought of sorting. Now, here sorting couldn’t be used directly as 
coins were correspondingly associated with the monster’s power. So, for that, I 
thought of making pairs of arrays B and C and then sorting the pair according to first 
value, using comparator function. And then I could get the answer in O(nlogn) time 
by using binary search on array A, by finding values less than each element of array 
B. I did mess up a bit with this approach, as this got complicated and I couldn’t think 
of a better approach, but still, I could pass 8/10 test cases. 
Results were declared on 8th November 2022 and 8 students were shortlisted for the 
interview rounds!

3 
 
PPT Session (30-45 Minutes): 
The shortlisted students were invited to attend the online PPT Session at 8 am on 9th 
November 2022. It was held on Skype. The presenter explained almost everything about the 
company. The principles they follow, their work culture, the process of interview, etc. Make 
a note of everything, as it might be helpful for you in the interview rounds. After the PPT, the 
interviews were scheduled on the same day. 
Technical Interview (45 Minutes): 
It started at 9:30 am.  
The interview began with the introduction of the interviewer and of course, followed by my 
introduction.  
Most of the interviews begin with the standard ‘Tell me about yourself’ question. Be prepared for it 
and do mention the key points about yourself that you are confident of. Don’t brag unnecessarily as 
questions may arise from it. 
Next, he enquired about my favorite subject in CS fundamentals. To which I answered OS, 
the reason being I was very confident with OS.  
This question is your golden chance to create a first good impression and brag your confidence about 
your most prepared subject. Don’t mess up with this and be very sure of at least one of the CS 
fundamentals.  
OS: 
❖ What is deadlock? 
It’s better to answer the definition and also explain it clearly in layman’s terms. And if possible, 
provide an example for the same. 
❖ What are the methods to overcome deadlock? 
An Example is a must here. I explained all four methods with examples. It’s okay to forget methods, 
but try to answer as much as possible. 
 
The interviewer was very friendly and after OS he asked me my next favorite subject. To 
which I answered DBMS, as I was confident with it. 
DBMS: 
❖ What is SQL? (pretty basic) 
❖ What all SQL databases I am familiar with? 
Whenever asked for examples, make sure to mention only those examples, with which you are at least 
a bit familiar. Questions may arise from anywhere. I mentioned  MariaDB and MYSQL as I was 
familiar with MariaDB because it was in our coursework and I knew the basics of MYSQL. 
❖ Have you used SQL databases in the projects mentioned in the resume? 
I had used a NoSQL database in my project so, I mentioned about MongoDB. 
❖ Of course, the next question was SQL v/s NoSQL 
Whenever asked for comparison, make sure to highlight the key differences and try to add real world 
comparisons. 
❖ Why did you use NoSQL? 
I mentioned that I had to include unstructured data(images and videos) in my project and also the 
benefits of NoSQL. He was quite satisfied with my answer. 
❖ Further, he asked me about Joins and Different types of Joins.

4 
 
Be prepared for the most common questions, make notes while studying, and revise them thoroughly 
before your interview. I could answer it well as I had revised it the last night. 
 
Then he moved on to Data Structures and Algorithms (the most important of all) 
So, he started with a pretty basic question:  
❖ How to reverse an array in place (i.e without using any extra space) 
It’s nice to start with brute force, but when clearly mentioned stick to it and start with what’s asked. I 
answered the swap method (loop through half of the array and swap every element with (n-i-1) 
element.) He was satisfied with this answer. 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/write-a-program-to-reverse-an-array-or-string/ 
 
❖ Then he asked me to count the occurrence of a character in the given string 
I messed up a bit with this pretty simple question. I directly jumped on to Hash Maps, which weren’t 
needed at all here. Soon after realizing, I corrected myself and gave the very basic approach of looping 
through the string.  
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-count-occurrence-given-character-string/  
 
Then he moved on to linked lists. 
❖  How to detect a cycle in a linked list? 
A pretty standard Linked list question. Again, started with brute force approach, hashing method and 
then explained the fast-slow pointer method (hare and tortoise method) 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/detect-loop-in-a-linked-list/ 
 
❖  Find (n-3)rd node from the given linked list.  
I started answering with the brute force approach: traverse the linked list and get the length of the list. 
Then, simply traverse to the (n-3)rd node as you now know n. Then he asked for a better approach. To 
which I explained the two-pointer approach. He was satisfied with this approach. 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nth-node-from-the-end-of-a-linked-list/ 
 
Then he moved on with Trees:  
❖ How to get the mirror image of a binary tree? 
I did mess up a little, as trees always confuse me a lot. I mentioned that I wasn’t much comfortable 
with trees, but still, I went on to answer and I answered it almost correctly and told the recursion 
method, used to swap left and right subtree.  
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/write-an-efficient-c-function-to-convert-a-tree-into-its-mirror-tree/ 
 
Note: I was asked to explain only the approach for all the questions. Depending on the 
interviewer, he/she might ask you to open up notepad or any editor and write down the 
pseudo-code for each question. 
 
He then went back to my Resume and asked me to explain one of the projects I had 
mentioned. This is most frequently asked. Make sure to answer this question in the STAR 
format. 
After this, before wrapping up, he finally asked me a few basic questions of OOPS. 
OOPS:

5 
 
Examples are a must to explain the concepts! 
❖ What are the Four Pillars of OOPs? 
This is the standard OOPs question, asked in most of the interviews. Be prepared for it with real world 
examples. I explained to him with real world examples and he was quite satisfied with it. 
❖ What is Inheritance and What are the types of Inheritance? 
Again, a very standard question. Revise well or else you may forget some types. I did forget to mention 
Hybrid Inheritance but recalled it with the help of the interviewer. 
Then he ended by asking if I had any questions. 
Always ask questions!!! I enquired about projects assigned to the interns and the tech stack used. Also, I asked 
about his experience with DB until now. It was a treat to hear about his journey! 
I did mess up a little, but it was the best interview out of the many interviews I had given 
previously. All round 1 interviews ended at 11:00 am since interviews were going on 
simultaneously. But the results were out almost after 2hrs. Anxiety levels rose up! 
Around 1:00 results were declared via mail and 3 students (including me) were shortlisted for 
Round 2. 
Professional Fitness Round (20 minutes): 
Only Deutsche Bank conducts this round, so we didn’t have much idea about this round. But 
through past experiences, I got to know that it is a sort of Technical + HR Round. 
It was scheduled to begin at 1:35 pm. But for me, it started a little late, almost at 1:45 pm, 
since the interviewer was busy with another interview.  
For me, this round was pretty basic, and to my surprise, there were no technical questions 
asked. She asked me to introduce myself and then went on to ask some HR questions. 
What is your dream? 
I started answering it from a career point of view. But she wanted to know my personal real 
dream! I answered it and we had a convincing discussion about it. 
She was very friendly and then asked me about my strengths and weaknesses. This question 
is asked to know what are you good at and how you handle your weaknesses. Always 
mention your strengths confidently and answer your weaknesses along with the way you are 
working to improve them. This is a frequently asked HR question. Be prepared and have 
pointers in your mind! 
She then asked me about my previous interview and then ended this interview as we were 
running out of time. 
She ended it up with Do you have any questions? I had asked her about the work culture at 
DB. For me, this round ended up within 15 minutes. 
This round totally depends on your interviewer. Basically, anything could be asked out here, 
it may be technical, it may be HR, or may be a mixture of both! 
Then again I thought they will take time to roll out the results for the next round. This time, I 
didn’t want the anxiety to rise. So, I just sat back and relaxed for a while. Then, around 3:30 
pm they mailed the results and all 3 of us were shortlisted for the HR Round.

6 
 
 
HR Round (15 minutes): 
It started at 3:45 pm. The interviewer greeted me and enquired about my experience in the 
past 2 rounds. Then she enquired about my family background and my future plans. We had a 
good discussion about it. After this, she asked me the standard question ‘Why Deutsche 
Bank?’ Make sure to have good information about the company you are interviewing for and 
the principles that the company follows. Most of the companies present themselves before the 
interviews with an interactive PPT session. Listen to it carefully and take the most advantage 
of it in the HR Round. After that, she asked me whether I had the documents that may be 
required for verification purposes (Aadhaar card, pan card and passport). This round ended 
well. 
The results were declared in the evening and the company hired all 3 of us for their summer 
internship program. 
 
Resources: 
DSA: 
Concept clearing: Abdul Bari’s DSA series 
Problem-Solving:  
It’s essential to solve and practice problems. Start this as soon as possible. While solving any 
problem, try to apply your logic and think of different test cases. Do not directly jump over to 
the solutions. Also, keep calculating the time and space complexity of each of your 
approaches and try optimizing it. 
There are various platforms for problem-solving, you can use any of them. But, my personal 
opinion would be to start  with some basic platforms like Hackerrank and gain some 
confidence in yourself, and then move on to Leetcode.  
Leetcode has a great variety of problems. You can try daily challenges, weekly and biweekly 
contests. Start with easy questions for each topic. But, then shift on to medium level 
questions and then finally a few hard questions.  
Don’t overwhelm yourself with medium or hard questions directly. But also, do not stick to 
easy questions. It is better to have a ratio of 3:6:1 or 3:5:2 for easy, medium and hard 
questions respectively. 
Also, quality matters over quantity! Give time to each question you solve( at least 5-10 
minutes of pondering over it), dry run it and then finally code it. 
For standard interview questions, you can follow various SDE sheets: 
Striver’s SDE Sheet (180 questions): https://takeuforward.org/interviews/strivers-sde-sheet-
top-coding-interview-problems/ 
Love Babbar SDE Sheet (450 questions): https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa-sheet-by-love-
babbar/

7 
 
I started with DSA very late, so I solved  Striver’s SDE Sheet. I would recommend starting 
DSA well in advance and if you have 3-4 months at least try solving Love Babbar’s SDE 
sheet as it covers almost every important interview question from various companies. There 
are other resources too, which you can check out! 
Also, GFG company archives are very helpful. If you are sure about your coding assessment, 
you can try solving that particular company archives to have a notch in interviews.  
 
❖ In the rest of the CS Fundamentals, make sure that all your concepts are very clear 
and I would recommend making notes for each of them, as they are very useful for 
last minute revision and are helpful in coursework too! 
OS: 
For OS, I followed the Gate Smashers playlist on YouTube. 
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxCzCOWd7aiGz9donHRrE9I3Mwn6XdP8p 
This is time-consuming, but it also helped me with coursework. You can follow other 
tutorials online. GFG also has good OS tutorials. 
DBMS: 
Here, it is very important to clear all the concepts and also to practice queries. 
Again, you can follow Gate Smashers. 
Start practicing queries on any of the platforms. I solved a few queries on Hackerrank and 
then on Leetcode too. 
 
OOPS: 
I studied OOPs from various platforms: Tutorialspoint, GFG, YT, and W3Schools. Make sure 
to have all concepts crystal clear in your mind. 
There is quite some difference between OOPs in Java and OOPs in C++. Make a note of it as 
they may be asked.  
In case you do not have your notes, this could be used for last-minute revision. I would 
suggest referring to this for revision purposes. It is a compilation of all OOPs concepts. 
https://whimsical.com/object-oriented-programming-cheatsheet-by-love-babbar-
YbSgLatbWQ4R5paV7EgqFw 
 
Confidence is the key for cracking interviews! 
Believe in yourself! 
ALL THE BEST.
